pyproject.toml:47 pins pandas>=2.0,<4; requirements.txt:79 pins 3.1.0. DataFrame.isetitem was added in pandas 1.5, so it exists across the allowed range. masking.py:157-164 collects integer positions via enumerate(df.columns) and calls masked.isetitem(i, Series) per position. isetitem is positional (iloc-style), so it replaces only that column and leaves duplicate-labelled siblings alone. The replacement Series uses index=df.index, so it is identical to the frame's index and needs no realignment, even if the index has duplicates. This rests on pandas' documented behavior, not on a run.

Compared masking.py:63-124 with issue-context.md lines 35-37. split_label_words splits on non-alnum chars (99-112). _split_chunk (71-96) groups chars into U/L/D runs, which gives lower-to-upper boundaries and letter/digit boundaries. For a U run followed by an L run it splits before the last capital (89-91), so APIKey gives api, key. The acronym exception (86-87) keeps a single 's' when the L run is exactly 's' and it is at the chunk end (end of label or before a non-alnum char) or before a digit. This matches 'end of label or before a non-letter', so PINs gives pins, and PINs2 and PINs_x also keep the s. password2 gives password, 2. Words are lowercased. _word_matches (115-116) accepts only equality, +s or +es, as the rule states. _label_matches (119-124) requires consecutive in-order words. Configured entries use the same split_label_words (137). I found no counterexample.
